long_description:
The physical economy still operates without a common language. Enterprise systems, factories, trucks, and robots generate enormous amounts of data, but most remains fragmented across legacy software and incompatible formats. Without a shared understanding of what is happening, even the most advanced AI cannot reliably coordinate how goods are made, moved, and delivered.

Oway is building that common language. Our protocol, IOI, connects enterprise systems and physical hardware, cleaning messy legacy data and live telemetry into a standardized schema that AI can understand and act on. Through a shared API, businesses can query their operations, identify inefficiencies, and automate actions across systems without replacing their existing software.

Our first model, Juno, applies this intelligence to unused truck capacity. It tracks empty space on trucks and sells it at a 50% discount to businesses shipping in the same direction. By moving freight directly on trucks already making the trip, Oway reduces shipping costs, damage, and transit times while generating additional revenue for carriers.

Every connected system and shipment expands our understanding of capacity, pricing, routes, facilities, and industrial operations. As this network grows, Oway is building toward a future where enterprise software, automated factories, self-driving vehicles, and robots can communicate and coordinate through one shared layer, making the physical economy programmable.
name: Oway
one_liner: The coordination OS for the physical economy.

long_description:
No Logo is building the orchestration layer for creating viral consumer products. The manufacturing world is full of capable, underutilized overseas factories with the machines, tooling, and engineers to build winning products – but no way to connect them to the creators and brands with the ideas and distribution. As a result, bringing a new product to market has traditionally taken 6-12 months, tens of thousands of dollars, and a team of 20-30 people.

No Logo collapses that. Using generative AI, we take a creator's product idea, visualize it, break it into core components and manufacturing processes, and match each step to the right factory in our network – turning an idea into a shippable product in just a few weeks.
name: No Logo
one_liner: Turn ideas into physical products

long_description:
Rebulk builds AI-native software for rail, transload, and bulk operations. We help teams manage railcars and trucks, transloading, maintenance, yard switching, railcar tracking, bulk inventory, documents, customer reporting, and billing.

Much of this work still runs on spreadsheets, paper tickets, phone calls, and disconnected legacy systems. That means teams spend too much time entering the same information twice, tracking down paperwork, figuring out where railcars and inventory are, and putting together reports by hand. Rebulk brings that work into modern software built around how each business actually operates.

We’ve lived this problem, and we know how to build for it. Warren previously led product at a Series A supply chain software startup, where he worked closely with companies moving and managing bulk commodities. Cole was engineer #3 at Tropic, helping scale it from seed to Series B, and later led engineering at an AI startup.

Rebulk runs operations at Venezia Transport, Usher Transport, Cicada Logistics, McDonald Farms, and TransloadX across transloading, rail maintenance, switching, railcar tracking, and bulk inventory.
name: Rebulk
one_liner: AI-native software for managing rail and bulk operations.

long_description: Fleetline is building the first complete-context algorithmic load planner for mid to large-sized trucking fleets. Today’s dispatchers face an overwhelming task: balancing regulations, customer demands, live fleet data, and individual driver needs, all while coordinating across siloed tools and teams. Mistakes run rampant, and each mistake is thousands of dollars. Even the select fleets using algorithms that have fleet-wide context struggle: the outputs are rigid, hard to interpret, and are blind to real-world nuances like driver preferences and schedule exceptions. Fleetline solves this by combining advanced optimization with LLMs that can easily adapt algorithms to each fleet’s needs and capture driver-specific information. The result is smarter planning truly optimized for every fleet and its drivers.
name: Fleetline
one_liner: Optimizing fleet planning with data driven algorithms

long_description:
Food Supply Chain companies have been using legacy ERPs for decades. Everyone knows these are necessary evils that essentially run the business but take up a lot of operational capacity. They are not about to just rip and replace their existing system that runs their whole business with a system that takes years to implement. Imagine if they could implement AI that runs the ERP for them, in weeks?

Burnt’s building an agentic OS for the Food Supply Chain with AI Agents for each department. 

Our AI Agent, Ozai, has started by replacing the whole order management job function at food distribution companies, so that sales and customer service teams can focus on what matters - the customer. Ozai monitors all incoming messages (emails, phone calls, voicemails, whatsapp, fax etc.), figures out if it's an order, learns each customer's habits, shorthand, and favorite products, picks up on any prep notes, and enters it straight into the existing ERP. It'll even go back to the customers on your behalf when it's not sure about something, clarify things and carry on working. 

The more it sees, the smarter it gets.
name: burnt
one_liner: Agentic Operating System for Food Supply Chain

long_description:
Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. You buy from Donkey: one contract, one company responsible for everything between the factory floor and your door. Our own people check the cartons before the factory gets paid, and the balance is due when the goods are accepted at your dock.

Small businesses buy imports through three or four middlemen, each adding 15 to 30 points, because none of them can fill a container on their own. Big enough to buy pallets, never big enough to buy the box. Quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs and live 15 to 30 days.

A trading company is rooms of people on the phone with factories, forwarders and brokers. Donkey runs that as one engine. It finds the real factory behind the customs record, stacks duty line by line, packs the container on weight and cube, and returns one number that holds from signature. Next comes the shared container: small buyers fill one box together at container prices, and every container earns better factory terms for the next one.

Team in San Francisco and Wuhan, English and Mandarin. If your business buys pallets of anything imported, send us your buying list.
name: Donkey
one_liner: The AI-native trading company: factory prices, delivered, one number

long_description:
Tarifflo is the infrastructure layer for modern customs - AI-powered filing, tariff recovery, and customs intelligence on one platform.

Filing should be free. Legacy ABI software charges you per entry, per user, per module. Brokers charge for every transaction. Tarifflo's filing software costs nothing - file directly with CBP under companies own filer codes.

We make money when our clients do. 1 in 8 entries has an error that overpays duty - misclassification, tariff stacking, valuation, origin. Most importers never catch them. Our AI audits your entries, finds the overpayments, and helps file for your refund. 

Under both is the same engine, live tariff intelligence covering every HTS code, Chapter 99 program, exclusion, and rate change - so the duty you pay going forward is as right as the refunds we recover looking back.
name: Tarifflo Inc.
one_liner: Supply chain compliance and cost savings
